title: 5 Days Solo in Mexico City: Street Food, Museums & Mezcal
description: Your personalized solo Mexico City itinerary with specific restaurants, hidden gems, and local tips.

days.title: Aztec Ruins, Street Tacos & Rooftop Mezcal
days.description: Ease into CDMX in the historic core — Aztec ruins, Diego Rivera murals, the best street food on earth, and mezcal with a view of the cathedral.

activities.name: Explore the Heart of the City
activities.description: Start at the Zócalo, one of the world's largest public plazas. Walk into the Palacio Nacional (free, bring ID) to see Diego Rivera's epic murals spanning Mexican history. Then head next door to Templo Mayor — the excavated main temple of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlán, sitting right in the middle of the modern city. The museum is excellent and manageable solo in 1–1.5 hours.

activities.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes & Mercado San Juan
activities.description: Walk to the jaw-dropping Palacio de Bellas Artes — even if you skip the museum inside, the Art Nouveau/Art Deco building is stunning. Then head to Mercado San Juan, the city's legendary gourmet market where chefs shop. Perfect for solo grazing — just point and eat.

activities.name: Mezcal, Views & Los Cocuyos
activities.description: Head to Balcón del Zócalo for sunset mezcal cocktails overlooking the cathedral and the lit-up Zócalo. Solo at a rooftop bar is a CDMX rite of passage. Then walk to Los Cocuyos, the legendary late-night taco stand that's been serving suadero and lengua since the 1950s.

days.title: Coffee Culture, Al Pastor & Cocktail Bars
days.description: Explore CDMX's trendiest neighborhoods — tree-lined streets, world-class restaurants, and the best al pastor trompo in the city. Roma and Condesa are made for wandering solo.

activities.name: Roma Norte Coffee Culture
activities.description: Start with coffee at Chiquitito Café, a tiny beloved third-wave spot in Roma Norte. Then stroll down tree-lined Álvaro Obregón with its sculptures and fountains. Pop into Librería Rosario Castellanos (a gorgeous two-story bookshop in a converted cinema) — amazing for a solo morning.

activities.name: Art Deco Architecture & the City's Best Seafood
activities.description: Walk into Condesa and spend the afternoon in Parque México — dogs everywhere, Art Deco buildings along Avenida México, street performers. Stop at Churrería El Moro for churros and hot chocolate. Then make your way to Contramar for a solo lunch at the bar.

activities.name: Taquería Orinoco & El Vilsito
activities.description: Tonight is about one thing: finding your al pastor soulmate. Start at Taquería Orinoco for Monterrey-style tacos and a lively vibe. Then Uber to El Vilsito — a mechanic shop by day, taco stand by night. This is peak CDMX. End with cocktails at Licorería Limantour.

days.title: Frida, Floating Gardens & Pulque
days.description: Adventure day — Frida Kahlo's blue house, floating through ancient Aztec canals on a trajinera, and the bohemian soul of Coyoacán. Saturday means Xochimilco will be lively and festive.

activities.name: Frida Kahlo Museum & Mercado de Coyoacán
activities.description: Book your Casa Azul (Frida Kahlo Museum) tickets online in advance — they sell out fast. The blue house is intimate and moving. After, wander the cobblestone streets of Coyoacán to the Mercado de Coyoacán for tostadas. Don't miss the Jardín Centenario plaza with its coyote fountain.

activities.name: Trajinera Ride on Ancient Canals
activities.description: Uber to Xochimilco's Embarcadero Nativitas (~30 min). Hire a trajinera (colorful flat-bottom boat). Solo tip: you can share a boat with other groups to split the cost, or hire your own small one. Vendors in smaller boats sell corn, beer, flowers, and mariachi. Budget 2–3 hours. Saturday is the liveliest day — other boats will pull up alongside yours.

activities.name: Pulque, Oaxacan Food & Night Vibes
activities.description: Head back to Coyoacán for the evening. Dinner at Corazón de Maguey for incredible Oaxacan cuisine, then hop to La Bipo for pulque — the ancient fermented agave drink. Saturday night Coyoacán is buzzing.

days.title: Pyramids of the Sun & Moon
days.description: Day trip to the ancient city of Teotihuacán — one of the largest archaeological sites in the Americas. You'll climb pyramids, walk the Avenue of the Dead, and feel genuinely small in the best way.

activities.name: Bus to Teotihuacán
activities.description: Take an early Uber to Terminal Autobuses del Norte (TAPO North). Autobuses Teotihuacán departs every 15 min from Gate 8 — no reservation needed, just buy at the counter. The ride is ~1 hour. Aim to arrive by 9am before the crowds and heat.

activities.name: Pyramid of the Sun, Moon & Avenue of the Dead
activities.description: Start at the Pyramid of the Sun — the third-largest pyramid in the world. The climb is steep (248 steps) and the altitude makes it breathless, but the view from the top is unforgettable. Then walk the 2km Avenue of the Dead to the Pyramid of the Moon. The entire site takes 3–4 hours to explore properly. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and lots of water.

activities.name: Chill Evening & El Califa de León
activities.description: You'll be tired from the pyramids. Head back to the city, shower, and keep the evening low-key. Walk to El Califa de León for what many consider the best bistec tacos in the city — a Michelin Bib Gourmand spot that's just a humble street taquería.

days.title: Museum, Castle & Farewell Feast
days.description: Your final day mixes world-class culture with a splurge-worthy farewell meal. Note: Mondays many museums are closed, but the Anthropology Museum and Chapultepec Castle are open.

activities.name: The World's Greatest Anthropology Museum
activities.description: This is Mexico's most-visited museum for good reason. The Aztec Sun Stone, Maya jade masks, Olmec heads — it's overwhelming in the best way. Solo travelers: rent the audio guide ($70 MXN) — it's genuinely excellent and makes the experience richer. Focus on the Mexica (Aztec) and Maya halls. Budget 2–3 hours.

activities.name: Chapultepec Castle, Museo Soumaya & Farewell Lunch
activities.description: Walk uphill to Chapultepec Castle — the only royal castle in the Americas. Panoramic views of Paseo de la Reforma are incredible. Then stroll through Polanco to Museo Soumaya (free, incredible art collection in a futuristic building). End with a farewell lunch at one of the world's best restaurants.

activities.name: Sunset Stroll & One Last Round
activities.description: Take a final evening walk down Paseo de la Reforma — the Ángel de la Independencia glows golden at sunset. End your trip back in Roma for one last round at your favorite taquería, or grab a mezcal nightcap at Pare de Sufrir, a hidden speakeasy in Roma Norte.
